import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# --- Data Cleaning and Feature Engineering ---

# Drop rows with missing income, which are crucial for this plot
df.dropna(subset=['Income'], inplace=True)

# For better visualization, remove a few extreme income outliers
df = df[df['Income'] < 200000].copy()

# Create a 'Total_Spending' column by summing all 'Mnt' (amount spent) columns
mnt_cols = [col for col in df.columns if 'Mnt' in col]
df['Total_Spending'] = df[mnt_cols].sum(axis=1)

# Create a 'Household_Status' column for easier segmentation based on children/teens
df['Household_Status'] = ((df['Kidhome'] + df['Teenhome']) > 0).map({True: 'With Children/Teens', False: 'No Children/Teens'})

# --- Visualization ---

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

# Create the lmplot (a figure-level function that combines regplot and FacetGrid)
# This is ideal for showing regression trends for different subsets of data
g = sns.lmplot(
    data=df,
    x='Income',
    y='Total_Spending',
    hue='Household_Status',
    height=8,
    aspect=1.5,
    scatter_kws={'alpha': 0.5, 's': 40, 'edgecolor': 'w'},
    line_kws={'lw': 2.5},
    legend=False # We will create a custom legend for better placement and title
)

# --- Customization and Labeling ---

# Access the underlying axes
ax = g.ax

# Set title and labels with more descriptive text
ax.set_title(
    'Impact of Dependents on Customer Spending by Income',
    fontsize=20,
    fontweight='bold',
    pad=25
)
ax.set_xlabel('Annual Household Income', fontsize=14, labelpad=10)
ax.set_ylabel('Total Spending (All Product Categories)', fontsize=14, labelpad=10)

# Format axis ticks to be more readable (e.g., $50K)
formatter = mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda x, p: f'${x/1000:.0f}K')
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(formatter)
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(formatter)
ax.tick_params(axis='both', which='major', labelsize=12)

# Add a custom, well-placed legend
ax.legend(
    title='Household Status',
    title_fontsize='13',
    fontsize='12',
    loc='upper left',
    frameon=True,
    shadow=True
)

# Add an insightful annotation to highlight the key takeaway
ax.annotate(
    'At any given income level, households with\nno children or teens tend to spend more.',
    xy=(100000, 1000),
    xytext=(115000, 1800),
    fontsize=12,
    bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.5", fc="aliceblue", ec="black", lw=1),
    arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", connectionstyle="arc3,rad=0.1", color='black')
)

# Adjust plot limits to provide some padding
ax.set_xlim(0, df['Income'].max() * 1.05)
ax.set_ylim(0, df['Total_Spending'].max() * 1.05)

# Save the final figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
